article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Indica-dominant hybrid
Genetics: Holland’s Hope × Super Skunk × Big Skunk Korean
Breeder: Soma’s Sacred Seeds
THC Content: 18%–23%
CBD Content: Generally low, usually below 1%
Terpene Profile: Caryophyllene , Limonene , Pinene
Primary Flavors: Sweet cherry, citrus, berry, floral notes
Flowering Time (Indoor): Approximately 9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: Late September to early October
Indoor Yield: Moderate to high
Outdoor Yield: High under favorable conditions
Grow Difficulty: Easy to moderate

Some marijuana strains earn their reputation through extreme potency, others through unusual flavor, but Reclining Buddha became memorable by combining several qualities that rarely arrive together so neatly. The flowers can carry a surprisingly sweet cherry-and-fruit character despite unmistakable old-school Skunk genetics, while the high starts brighter and more mentally animated than the plant’s indica-heavy appearance might suggest.

Gradually, that lively beginning gives way to a comfortable body calm that explains the unusually appropriate name. Created by Soma Seeds during an earlier period of Dutch cannabis breeding , this cultivar also predates today’s obsession with dessert crosses and candy terpenes, giving it an identity rooted in classic Skunk vigor, outdoor resilience, resin production, and a relaxed but still mentally engaging experience.
Genetics and Lineage

Soma Seeds developed Reclining Buddha as a three-way hybrid involving Holland’s Hope, Super Skunk, and Big Skunk Korean. Soma’s historical description of that combination notes that Holland’s Hope was already circulating in the Netherlands during the 1980s and had earned a reputation for compact structure and dependable performance in damp outdoor conditions. Super Skunk contributed additional flower density and classic pungency, while Big Skunk Korean expanded the aromatic and psychoactive character of the final selection. The cultivar was also historically known as Soma Skunk V before acquiring its more recognizable name.

Each branch of the pedigree contributes something practical. Holland’s Hope helps explain why the plant has long been recommended for growers dealing with unstable outdoor weather and higher humidity. Super Skunk strengthens the familiar skunky, earthy foundation while encouraging robust flowers, and Big Skunk Korean adds another layer of fruitiness and effect complexity. Soma later used Reclining Buddha as important breeding material of his own; Buddha’s Sister , for example, combines Reclining Buddha with Afghani Hawaiian, and Soma’s current breeder description specifically refers back to the sweeter character of Reclining Buddha.
Effects and Experience

The experience is more animated at first than the name “Reclining Buddha” might lead someone to expect. A light cerebral rush can arrive relatively early, bringing a brighter mood and a tendency for ordinary situations to feel more entertaining. Conversation may become easier, humor lands more readily, and music or creative hobbies can hold attention without producing the intensely driven quality of a pure sativa. Historical strain descriptions consistently emphasize this unusual combination of a mentally clear or euphoric beginning with an indica-dominant physical foundation.

Physical relaxation becomes increasingly important as the high matures. Tension may begin fading through the neck, shoulders, and limbs while the early mental activity settles into a calmer rhythm. At a moderate dose, experienced consumers may still feel sociable and mentally present, making the strain appropriate for an unhurried evening rather than immediate sleep. Increase the amount, however, and the balance can shift strongly toward heaviness, stillness, and a desire to remain seated. That progression gives this cultivar more range than a simple “sedating indica” label would suggest.

Potency should be treated as variable rather than fixed. Contemporary strain references commonly place THC somewhere around the high teens to low 20s, while individual cultivation methods and phenotypes can move results in either direction. Consumers with limited tolerance should therefore start conservatively. Excessive THC can produce dry mouth, dry eyes, dizziness, paranoia, or an uncomfortable increase in mental intensity rather than additional relaxation.
Medical Benefits

For medical marijuana consumers, the strain’s gradual transition from cerebral uplift to body relaxation may be useful when stress and physical discomfort occur together. The early change in mood can temporarily make persistent worries or mental fatigue feel less dominant, while the later physical phase may make soreness, headaches, or muscular tension less intrusive. Some consumers also find heavier servings more compatible with nighttime use because the initially social quality eventually gives way to quieter physical comfort. These observations describe commonly reported cannabis experiences rather than proven strain-specific medical effects.

Reclining Buddha has not been clinically demonstrated to treat pain, anxiety, depression , inflammation , insomnia, or any other disorder. Research on cannabis and cannabinoids more broadly suggests that some THC/CBD-containing products can produce modest short-term benefits for certain types of chronic pain, but dizziness and sleepiness are among the possible adverse effects. Evidence regarding anxiety is limited, and THC-rich cannabis can produce unwanted psychological effects in some individuals.

Sleep is similarly complicated. Studies involving cannabinoids sometimes show improved sleep in people who have other medical conditions, but it remains uncertain whether cannabis directly improves sleep or simply reduces another symptom that had been interfering with rest. Anyone using weed therapeutically should therefore consider dose, personal tolerance, medications, and professional medical guidance instead of assuming that a strain name guarantees a particular clinical result.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Sweetness is one of the cultivar’s more surprising traits. Historical Soma-related descriptions emphasize a sweet cherry-candy character, while other references describe pungent Skunk layered with fruit, berries, and flowers. Open a properly cured jar and the first impression may lean toward ripe cherry or mixed fruit before an earthier, unmistakably cannabis-like background begins to appear. Once the flower is broken apart, citrus peel, herbs, soil, and skunky spice can become considerably stronger.

Reported terpene information is less standardized than the genetic history, so no single terpene formula should be treated as definitive. Available profiles commonly point toward caryophyllene and limonene, with pinene appearing as a supporting compound. Caryophyllene is consistent with the drier pepper-and-spice qualities, limonene complements the citrus sweetness, and pinene can contribute a cleaner herbal or pine-like edge. Actual laboratory results can vary according to phenotype, growing environment, harvest maturity, and curing technique.

Flavor develops from sweet toward savory. Cherry, berries, lemon, and orange-like citrus can appear on the inhale, followed by floral notes and a distinctly earthy Skunk finish. Unlike modern candy weed, the sweetness does not completely dominate the smoke. A properly finished sample retains enough soil, herbs, and old-school pungency to reveal its Skunk ancestry after the fruit fades.
Growing Information

Reclining Buddha gained part of its reputation from being unusually practical outdoors. Holland’s Hope contributes resilience in damp weather, while the plant generally develops a sturdy, compact, indica-influenced structure with strong branching. Historical grow information describes good resistance to humidity and weather fluctuations, making the cultivar more forgiving than many dense-flowering varieties in climates where autumn conditions are not perfectly dry. It can also be cultivated indoors without demanding excessive vertical space.

Indoor flowering takes roughly nine weeks, and patience matters near the finish. Soma’s historical description noted that the pistils can darken relatively early, making the flowers appear mature before the plant has actually reached its best finishing point. Allowing the complete flowering period gives the buds additional time to develop resin and their characteristic aroma. Low-stress training can spread the naturally compact structure, while a slightly longer vegetative period may be useful when growers want a larger, more extensively branched plant.

Outdoor plants commonly mature around late September under appropriate Northern Hemisphere conditions, with productive individuals capable of substantial yields. Even though the genetics carry useful humidity tolerance, dense cannabis flowers should never be treated as immune to mold. Air movement, canopy spacing, and routine inspection remain important as buds gain mass. Growers should determine final maturity by looking at trichomes, calyx development, and the plant’s overall progression rather than harvesting simply because the pistils have darkened.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Reclining Buddha?
Soma Seeds created the cultivar from Holland’s Hope, Super Skunk, and Big Skunk Korean. Historical breeder descriptions consistently identify it as a three-way hybrid combining those genetic lines.
Who bred Reclining Buddha?
Reclining Buddha was created by Soma Seeds, also known as Soma’s Sacred Seeds. The variety was historically called Soma Skunk V before becoming better known under its current name.
Is Reclining Buddha indica or sativa?

It is generally considered an indica-dominant hybrid. Its physical effects become strongly relaxing, although the beginning can retain enough sativa influence to feel euphoric, sociable, creative, or mentally clear.
What does Reclining Buddha taste like?
Expect a combination of sweet cherry, berries, citrus, floral notes, earth, and classic Skunk pungency. Some examples emphasize fruit considerably more strongly than others.
How long does Reclining Buddha take to flower?

Approximately nine weeks indoors is the traditional benchmark. Outdoor plants are commonly ready around late September in suitable climates, although actual harvest timing depends on environment and plant maturity.
Final Thoughts on Reclining Buddha

Reclining Buddha represents a style of cannabis breeding that feels increasingly distinct from the genetics dominating modern dispensaries. Instead of stacking Gelato , Cookies , Zkittlez , or Runtz ancestry, Soma worked with older Dutch, Skunk, and Korean-derived material to produce marijuana whose character revolves around resilience, fruit-and-Skunk terpenes, resin, and a genuinely evolving high. The plant begins with enough cerebral brightness to remain interesting before settling naturally into the relaxed physical state suggested by its name.

Its continued relevance also comes from practicality. A nine-week flowering period, compact structure, useful outdoor durability, and respectable production make the cultivar more than a historical curiosity. Flavor-focused consumers get sweet cherry and citrus without losing the earthy pungency of classic weed, while experienced growers gain access to genetics that reflect an important chapter of Soma Seeds history. For anyone exploring influential cultivars from the period before modern dessert cannabis took over the market, Reclining Buddha remains an unusually distinctive intersection of Skunk vigor, fruity sweetness, and deep evening relaxation.
